chunks: Ahmad ibn Ziyad ibn Ja'far al-Hamadani (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashem narrated to him, saying: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Hasani narrated to me, saying:

Al-Ma'mun sent a young girl to Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him). When she was brought in, she expressed dislike at his white hair. When he saw her dislike, he returned her to Al-Ma'mun and wrote to him with these verses:

White hair announces to my soul that youth has passed to its farthest end. I shall weep for it and lament it at length, but alas, what is gone will not return. The beautiful women fear the whiteness of my head; I see the fair ones avoiding me. If youth, my beloved, has departed, I shall accompany it with God-consciousness until... And at old age, the wise take heed, yet I do not see its place returning. I call it to me, hoping it answers, while my lying soul tempts me with it. Whoever lives long grows old, and in their leaving us is our portion. Indeed, white hair is also my beloved, until the near deadline separates us.
ai.seo_question: What poem did Imam al-Rida compose when a girl disliked his white hair?
ai.summary: This narrative from *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida* illustrates Imam al-Rida’s (a.s.) dignified response to Caliph Al-Ma'mun’s political gifting, using the girl’s aversion to his graying hair as a metaphor for the transient nature of worldly youth. The accompanying poem elevates the physical signs of aging into spiritual maturity, emphasizing that *taqwa* (piety) remains the true companion of the believer as time passes. This event highlights the Imam’s mastery of silence and subtle wisdom in navigating the Abbasid court's scrutiny.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 43-8 Ahmad ibn Ziyad al-Hamadani - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashem quoted on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Muhammad Al-Hassani, “Al-Ma’mun sent a young girl to Abil Hassan Ar-Ridha’ (a.s.). Upon entering, she expressed her dislike of his white hair. When the Imam (a.s.) noticed this he returned her to Al-Ma’mun with the following poem that he (a.s.) himself composed:

My white hair informs me of the approach of my deathAt old age one accepts adviceYes, indeed youth passed and has ended nowAnd I will never experience its returnI cry and weep over it having gone byAnd keep on calling it perhaps it hears my callAh! What I have lostMy lying self forces me to want it backBeautiful women fear my white hairBut whoever stays too long will get oldI see the beautiful silver-colored women running away from me.Now my share is their separation from meIf youth which has now gone by was my beloved friendNow it is old age that is my friendI will be in its company with piety untilThe soon to arrive death separates us!
